{"code": "import numpy as np

# Re-check the missing rows to confirm they are not systematically different
# Specifically, check if the complete cases have similar distributions

# Drop rows with missing flipper_length_mm or body_mass_g
complete_data = df.dropna(subset=['flipper_length_mm', 'body_mass_g'])

# Get the two missing rows
missing_rows = df[df['flipper_length_mm'].isnull() | df['body_mass_g'].isnull()]

# Print the values in the missing rows for these two variables
print("Missing rows (flipper_length_mm and body_mass_g):")
print(missing_rows[['species', 'island', 'flipper_length_mm', 'body_mass_g']])

# Compare the mean of flipper_length_mm and body_mass_g in complete cases
print(f"\nMean flipper length (complete cases): {complete_data['flipper_length_mm'].mean():.2f}")
print(f"Mean body mass (complete cases): {complete_data['body_mass_g'].mean():.2f}")

# Since the missing rows have no values, we can't compute their mean
# But we can check if the species and islands of the missing rows are representative
print(f"\nSpecies in missing rows: {missing_rows['species'].unique()}")
print(f"Island in missing rows: {missing_rows['island'].unique()}")

# Check the distribution of species and island in complete vs missing
print(f"\nSpecies distribution in complete cases: {complete_data['species'].value_counts(normalize=True)}")
print(f"Species distribution in missing rows: {missing_rows['species'].value_counts(normalize=True)}")
print(f"Island distribution in complete cases: {complete_data['island'].value_counts(normalize=True)}")
print(f"Island distribution in missing rows: {missing_rows['island'].value_counts(normalize=True)}")

# Compute the correlation
correlation = complete_data['flipper_length_mm'].corr(complete_data['body_mass_g'])
print(f"\nPearson correlation: {correlation:.4f}")"}
